brief: Nasdaq rose 2.9% over September 29th-October 6th on AI optimism, outperforming the S&P (+1.9%) and Russell 2k (+0.8%), with GS's AI Leaders and Broad AI baskets up 6.4% and 5.6% on infrastructure-agreement news. Nasdaq futures aggregate open interest rose in 3 of 5 sessions for a net $8.9bn, with the largest upticks on October 2nd and 5th alongside price strength, suggesting new long positioning. But Nasdaq 3-month funding cheapened in outright terms and moved sideways versus S&P funding, implying the OI build also reflected outright shorts and/or hedging rather than pure long initiation. Sponsorship from Asset Managers, the largest Non-Dealer cohort, looks questionable: their gross longs have generally declined since a nominal peak on June 2nd, and the historically positive correlation between Asset Manager gross long changes and price was nil as of the September 29th CFTC Commitment of Traders update. The note frames the rally's positioning support as unresolved rather than confirmed.
